Name: Atlit-Yam (עתלית ים)
Description: An ancient well, dated to the early 6th millennium BCE (5900 BCE), found submerged 10m below current sea level. It was a cylindrical shaft 1.5m in diameter and 5.7m deep, dug through clay and into kurkar. A second well was found 100m north, dug into clay and lined with stone.

Name: Khirbet Jarassur (ח'רבת ג'אראסור)
Description: A well found at a Halafian culture site (5200 BCE), considered by Campbell to be the oldest well in the world. Most of its upper part was destroyed during the excavation of an irrigation channel.
